interior.label: $T$ and $r$

markers.legend: the shell of charged dust, $r = R$

interior.input: The shell with $r_q = 0.48\,r_s$ and $\mu = 0.2\,r_s$, which comes in from infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light and turns round at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$. Its proper time from $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ to the turn is $0.39\,r_s/c$.
caption: The plane of $T$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) inside the shell, drawn for a shell that comes in from infinity with more charge than rest mass. The shell encloses no charge, so space is flat here: every ray runs at 45° and every cone is the same. The shell is the curve $r = R(T)$, a hyperbola's cousin, the path of a charge thrown at a fixed like charge in flat space. It turns round at $T = 0$ at $R = 0.317\,r_s$ and leaves at the speed it came in with.

The event horizon is the outgoing ray that reaches the shell as the shell crosses $r_+$, at $cT = -0.53\,r_s$; it leaves the centre at $cT = -1.17\,r_s$ and crosses flat space, where no local measurement marks it. The Cauchy horizon is the ingoing ray $cT + r = 0.50\,r_s$, which leaves the shell as it comes back up through $r_-$. An event above that ray can receive light from the singularity of the charged field outside.

interior.label: through the centre

markers.legend: the shell of charged dust, $r = R$

interior.input: The shell with $r_q = 0.48\,r_s$ and $\mu = 0.2\,r_s$, which comes in from infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light and turns round at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$. Its proper time from $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ to the turn is $0.39\,r_s/c$.
caption: The line through the centre of the shell in the plane $\theta = \pi/2$, from the shell to the shell: $x = r$ on the right is $\phi = 0$ and $x = -r$ on the left is $\phi = \pi$. The two sides of the shell close to $0.317\,r_s$ of the centre at $T = 0$ and open again. The event horizon is the pair of rays that leave the centre at $cT = -1.17\,r_s$, and the Cauchy horizon the pair that meet there at $cT = 0.50\,r_s$.

exterior.label: outside $r_+$

markers.legend: the shell of charged dust, $r = R$

exterior.input: The shell with $r_q = 0.48\,r_s$ and $\mu = 0.2\,r_s$, which comes in from infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light and turns round at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$. Its proper time from $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ to the turn is $0.39\,r_s/c$.
caption: The plane of $t$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) outside the shell and outside $r_+$, where the metric is Reissner-Nordström's. The edges of the cones are $dr/d(ct) = \pm(1 - r_s/r + r_q^2/r^2)$. Inside the shell, $r < R(t)$, lies the flat interior, which keeps a time of its own.

The shell reaches $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ only as $t \to \infty$, while its own clock passes $r_+$ at a finite reading, $0.39\,r_s/c$ before the turn. Its fall through both horizons lies beyond these coordinates, and the advanced time $v$ follows it there.

exterior.label: inside $r_-$

markers.legend: the shell of charged dust, $r = R$

exterior.input: The shell with $r_q = 0.48\,r_s$ and $\mu = 0.2\,r_s$, which comes in from infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light and turns round at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$. Its proper time from $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ to the turn is $0.39\,r_s/c$.
caption: The plane of $t$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) outside the shell and inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$, where $1 - r_s/r + r_q^2/r^2$ is positive again and $t$ is once more a time. The shell comes down from $r_-$ at $t \to -\infty$, turns round at $t = 0$ at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, and climbs back to $r_-$ as $t \to \infty$, all in a proper time of $0.27\,r_s/c$. The drawing holds the turn itself, the stretch of $t$ within $0.16\,r_s/c$ of it, in which the shell stays below $0.324\,r_s$.

The repulsion that turns it is the electric field's. The dust is at rest at the turn, where $\gamma = 1$, and the field energy outside the shell and the binding energy of the dust make up the rest of the mass seen from outside. Below the shell, $r < R(t)$, space is flat, so the singularity at $r = 0$ of the charged field is absent from this region.

exterior_ingoing.label: against $v - r$

markers.legend: the shell of charged dust, $r = R$

exterior_ingoing.input: The shell with $r_q = 0.48\,r_s$ and $\mu = 0.2\,r_s$, which comes in from infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light and turns round at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$. Its proper time from $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ to the turn is $0.39\,r_s/c$.
caption: The plane of $v$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) outside the shell, drawn with $v - r$ as the vertical axis so that the ingoing rays, $v$ constant, run at 45°. The shell crosses $r_+$ at $v = -0.02\,r_s$ and $r_-$ at $v = 0.11\,r_s$, and turns round at $v = 0.30\,r_s$ and $R = 0.317\,r_s$. Inside the shell, $r < R(v)$, space is flat.

Between the horizons every future cone points to smaller $r$, and inside $r_-$ the cones open upward again, which is where the shell turns. It climbs back toward $r_-$ and reaches it only as $v \to \infty$, so these coordinates end there, on the inner horizon it leaves through.

exterior_outgoing.label: against $u + r$

markers.legend: the shell of charged dust, $r = R$

exterior_outgoing.input: The shell with $r_q = 0.48\,r_s$ and $\mu = 0.2\,r_s$, which comes in from infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light and turns round at $R = 0.317\,r_s$, inside $r_- = 0.36\,r_s$. Its proper time from $r_+ = 0.64\,r_s$ to the turn is $0.39\,r_s/c$.
caption: The plane of $u$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) outside the shell, drawn with $u + r$ as the vertical axis so that the outgoing rays, $u$ constant, run at 45°. These coordinates take up where the ingoing ones end: the shell comes down from $r_-$ at $u \to -\infty$, turns round at $u = -0.30\,r_s$, and leaves through $r_-$ at $u = -0.11\,r_s$ and $r_+$ at $u = 0.02\,r_s$.

Between the horizons every future cone now points to larger $r$, a white hole, and the $r_+$ the shell comes out of bounds another exterior, with its own infinity. The shell leaves for that infinity at $0.92$ of the speed of light, the speed it came in with.

exterior_isotropic.label: the point charge
exterior_isotropic.input: The balanced shell, $b = 0$ and $\mu = a$, for which $r_q = r_s/2 = a$, at rest at the isotropic radius $\epsilon = a$, where its areal radius is $2a$.
caption: The plane of $t$ and $\rho$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) outside the balanced shell, whose charge and rest mass are equal, $\mu = r_q = a$. Such a shell stays at rest at any radius outside $r = a$, here at $\rho = \epsilon = a$, and the mass seen from outside is its rest mass whatever $\epsilon$ is. The edges of the cones are $d\rho/d(ct) = \pm(1 + a/\rho)^{-2}$.

Arnowitt, Deser, and Misner's point charge is the limit $\epsilon \to 0$. The areal radius of the shell, $\epsilon + a$, stays above $a$, while its distance from any sphere outside grows as $a\ln(1/\epsilon)$ and the cones close toward $\rho = 0$. In the limit the shell lies down a throat of radius $a$ and unbounded length.
